title: Deliver plumbline 0.0.3 agent contract
description: plumbline needs a safe, agent-first 0.0.3 release contract. The current command, output, configuration, and release behavior cannot yet prove that shipped documentation and current binary behavior agree before release.
design: Deliver the Foundation slices and Phases 1 through 6 in their declared order. Keep one registry as the source for parser declarations, introspection, schemas, and generated contract material. Keep machine output deterministic apart from declared volatile metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- All Foundation and Phase child tasks are complete in dependency order.
- `plumb` provides the declared 0.0.3 command, configuration, diagnostic, and release-safety behavior.
- The release verification bar passes, including tests, conformance, deterministic output checks, and a self-preflight.

title: Build registry-driven command core
description: Manual argument handling and separate output paths cannot provide complete, reliable agent responses. Every supported invocation needs one typed result path with a stable diagnostic order and a valid machine envelope on both success and failure.
design: Replace manual argv scanning with a registry-driven parser. Lexically detect `--json` only before `--` during bootstrap, then route parsing, config discovery, loading, and execution through one top-level handler. Add typed outcomes, the seven-key envelope renderer, help and version JSON forms, ANSI policy, exit and diagnostic registries, fixed diagnosis order, and near-match hints. Convert unexpected faults to `INTERNAL`, exit 6. Do not allow project I/O, direct printing, or process exit to bypass the handler.
acceptance_criteria:
- Global flags work before or after the verb and before `--`; tokens after `--` are raw arguments.
- The parser rejects unknown flags, bad arity, flag-shaped values, empty values, and conflicting color selectors at the declared diagnosis stage.
- Every `--json` success and failure is a single final-newline JSON value with all seven envelope keys; JSON stdout contains no diagnostics or ANSI.
- Help and version work without project configuration in human and JSON forms.
- Golden tests cover success, input error, safety block, environment error, conflict, transient error, and internal error envelopes.
notes: CLOSED: Replaced the manual command path with a typed parser and universal result renderer. Added JSON envelope, exit-class, help, version, and parser grammar coverage. See close reason for commits.
close_reason: Built the registry-ready command core, universal envelopes, exit dictionary, and binary grammar checks — commits 3217cc2 and e116355

title: Add safe release dry run
description: Users need to prove all read-only release checks before they create a tag or push it. The release command must provide this without publishing or changing repository state.
design: Add `release --dry-run`. Run the read-only release checks, full preflight, `cargo package --list`, and `cargo publish --dry-run --locked`. Do not tag, push, or publish. Treat `--yes --dry-run` as an invalid selector conflict. Sort package-file and push-ref data before serialization.
acceptance_criteria:
- A dry run makes no tag, push, or publish action and does not require `--yes`.
- A dry run exits as the equivalent real release would before its first state-changing step.
- Clean dry-run data has mode `dry-run`, skipped state-changing steps with reason `dry-run`, no completed state changes, and exactly one real release command.
- Failing dry runs return no suggested commands.
- Tests prove no mutation occurs and cover selector conflict, output ordering, and report semantics.

title: Generate CONTRACT.md tables
description: Committed contract tables can become stale when maintained separately from the live command registry. Documentation must be generated from the same declared command and diagnostic facts that agents discover at runtime.
design: Add `contract-doc <section>` for verbs, gates, exit codes, and error codes. Render table data directly from `CommandSpec` and the diagnostic registry. Emit raw UTF-8 Markdown outside JSON and an envelope with section and markdown under `--json`. Choose and record one generated-block layout in configuration, then validate it with the generated-block gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid contract sections render deterministic table Markdown from live registry data with no second data source.
- `contract-doc --json` returns section and markdown in the standard envelope; non-JSON mode emits declared raw UTF-8 Markdown only.
- An unknown section returns `INVALID_INPUT`, legal sections, and a near-match hint.
- CONTRACT.md generated blocks match live capabilities through the generated-block gate.
- Tests cover schemas, raw bytes, envelope, invalid selector, determinism, and self-generated blocks.

title: Add registry-backed introspection
description: Agents need one complete, live command contract. Separate parser, help, capability, schema, and guide definitions can drift and make discovery unreliable.
design: Define an in-process `CommandSpec` tree as the single source for command declarations. Generate the parser declarations, terse help, capabilities object, schema output, and robot guide from it. Add a parser-derived manifest comparison that fails when parser and capabilities surfaces differ. Start the contract version at `0.1` and change capabilities data from an array to an object.
acceptance_criteria:
- `capabilities --json` returns one envelope whose data contains the full declared command, flag, exit, error, environment, limit, configuration, schema, guide, and value-domain contract.
- Every verb declaration includes positionals, flags, output modes, exit codes, payload schema, meta fields, and examples.
- `schema --json` returns envelope and payload schemas; `--command` selects one declared verb path and rejects an unknown path with a legal set and correction hint.
- Terse help, capabilities, schema, and robot guide derive from `CommandSpec`.
- Manifest-parity and golden tests pin capabilities, schema, help, and initial payloads.
notes: CLOSED: CommandSpec now supplies command parsing, help, capability declarations, parser manifest, schema selection, and the robot guide. Added binary contract tests. See close reason for commit ref.

title: Protect mutations and release state
description: Capture and release can change repository state. They need explicit consent, atomic writes, and immutable release-tag handling so a retry cannot silently overwrite or hide prior state changes.
design: Require exactly one capture mode: `--check` for comparison or `--yes` for write. Require `--yes` for mutating capture and release operations. Use atomic writes. Model existing release tags as immutable conflicts except when local and remote state proves the exact release was already submitted from the current commit; report that case as idempotent success. Render human output from typed results rather than a second report model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bare capture fails with `MISSING_REQUIRED` and names `capture --check` and `capture --yes`.
- Capture modes are mutually exclusive; every state-changing path requires `--yes` and has no `--force` override.
- Writes are atomic and do not overwrite a different selected configuration or release tag.
- A proven completed release is an idempotent success; incomplete or conflicting tag state is an exit-5 conflict with a safe inspection or recovery command.
- Golden tests cover mutation refusal, completed-release no-op, and partial-release conflict results.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added `--yes` and `-y` grammar for capture and release, including missing-mode and selector-conflict failures.
- Made capture fixture and generated-document writes atomic with sibling temporary files, fsync, and rename.
- Added typed release results and immutable release-state checks. A retry succeeds only when identical local and remote annotated tags and the remote release branch all point to the current commit.
- Added mutation-refusal and release-state tests; the full test suite passes.

title: Implement safe config command family
description: Release-safety decisions depend on configuration, but callers cannot yet safely inspect, validate, or change a selected configuration with provenance and conflict protection.
design: Add `config schema`, `validate`, `show`, `get`, `set`, and `patch`. Resolve relative paths from the selected config's parent directory. Enforce JSON Schema validation, RFC 6901 pointer rules, canonical sorted-key compact JSON hashes, default and file provenance, and selection-source reporting. Implement `set` and JSON Merge Patch writes with a sibling advisory lock, strict `--if-match` precondition before no-op detection, fsync, and rename.
acceptance_criteria:
- Config discovery precedence is `--config`, then `PLUMB_CONFIG`, then the default path; output identifies the selected source and crate root.
- Schema validation rejects unknown keys and returns stable ordered errors with pointers, expected and actual value classes, remediation, and near-match hints.
- `show` and `get` return the full canonical config hash and declared provenance; nested values inherit their top-level provenance.
- `set` and `patch` require `--yes`, `--if-match`, and schema-valid results; patch reads exactly one UTF-8 JSON Merge Patch only with `--from-stdin`.
- Matching no-op writes succeed with `already_complete`; stale hashes fail before no-op detection; busy locks and write conflicts use their declared diagnostics.
- Golden tests cover provenance, pointer failures, updates, no-ops, stale-hash conflicts, invalid patch results, lock busy, and write conflicts.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added registry-backed `config schema`, `validate`, `show`, `get`, `set`, and `patch` commands.
- Added explicit, environment, and default config selection with selected-config parent-directory roots.
- Added canonical SHA-256 hashes, JSON Pointer access, inherited provenance, strict hash preconditions, advisory locks, and atomic config writes.
- Added command-level tests for selection precedence, guarded updates, no-op success, stale-hash conflict, patch input, missing pointers, invalid pointers, lock contention, and schema-safe writes.

Test builds run injected probes; release builds compile fault triggers out and report each injection case as not applicable with the fixed reason.

- One verdict set is pinned for each profile; a pass that changes to not applicable fails review until accepted.

title: Fail closed on config and manifest input
description: Malformed optional configuration and guessed Cargo manifest data can disable a release gate or produce false claims. Configuration and package input must fail closed before release decisions use them.
design: Validate every optional block by presence and type, then enforce cross-field coherence. Use a TOML parser for `package.include` and `package.exclude`; keep `cargo package --list` as the actual package-file source. Register configuration fields, domains, error codes, and payload schemas in capabilities. Regenerate the self-contract fixture through capture.
acceptance_criteria:
- Missing optional blocks use only documented defaults; null, scalar, array, and malformed values never act as absence.
- Claims require a fixture, generated blocks require capture, release requires a valid branch and remote, generated IDs are unique, and write paths stay within the crate root.
- Cargo manifest parsing reads only package include and exclude arrays; comments, strings, multiline arrays, and invalid TOML have correct behavior.
- Validation output is stable and includes selected config path, crate root, version, and validation errors; useful failure data remains available in JSON.
- Tests cover optional-block shapes, unknown keys, key near matches, precedence, path-root resolution, atomic-write failure, and manifest edge cases.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Made optional config fields fail closed for null, scalar, array, and malformed values.
- Enforced known top-level fields, config version, generated-ID uniqueness, strict nested generated shapes, allowed package allowlist values, and crate-root-relative write paths.
- Replaced guessed Cargo manifest parsing with a TOML parser for package include and exclude arrays.
- Added validation and TOML edge-case tests; the full suite passes.

title: Resolve capture artifacts from Cargo
description: Guessed executable paths fail for workspaces, custom target directories, profiles, and Windows. Capture must run the exact binary that Cargo reports.
design: Run the declared Cargo build invocation with Cargo JSON messages enabled without changing other semantic arguments. Parse compiler-artifact records and select the binary target whose name equals `capture.command[0]`; use its non-null executable path verbatim. Share one build and resolver across a generated-block batch.
acceptance_criteria:
- Configuration accepts only a non-empty Cargo build invocation with valid Cargo build selectors.
- Capture uses the matching binary compiler-artifact executable and never synthesizes a target path.
- Missing or ambiguous matching artifacts fail with observed candidates and an instruction to narrow `capture.build`.
- Capture and generated-block rendering use the same resolver and reuse one batch build.
- Tests cover workspace members, custom target directory, release profile, Windows executable path, missing artifact, and ambiguous artifact.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Required `capture.build` to be a Cargo build invocation.
- Added Cargo JSON compiler-artifact selection for the configured capture binary, including missing and ambiguous-artifact diagnostics.
- Capture and generated rendering now share the Cargo-reported executable for each capture batch.
- Updated the self capture command to request JSON output and verified the full suite plus a live capture freshness result.

title: Produce ordered preflight reports
description: Automation needs the full ordered release-gate result and safe next actions. A single flattened failure hides independent gate failures and state changes during a release attempt.
design: Define one ordered gate plan for preflight and the pre-tag release path. Always emit records for worktree cleanliness, fixture freshness, stray documentation blocks, packaged allowlist, and generated freshness; mark non-applicable gates as skipped. Add partial reports, deterministic data hashing, structured recommended actions, and explicit release step records with completed state changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preflight reports all declared gates in fixed order with passed, failed, or skipped status and closed skip reasons.
- A blocked preflight returns exit 2, `PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED`, a partial report, separate leaf diagnostics, and only safe paste-ready commands.
- Gate and release-step records have no wall-clock fields; aggregate elapsed time is excluded from goldens and report data hashes.
- Release reports preflight, release identity, ordered steps, and exact completed state changes; failures after tagging disclose local state.
- Tests cover pass, multiple independent failures, skips, clean JSON stdout, human rendering, state-change failure positions, and golden normalization.

title: Add structural stale-data diffs
description: Whole-document text differences do not give automation a stable or bounded description of stale fixtures and generated blocks. Agents need structural changes with precise locations.
design: Replace stale fixture and block text differences with one machine-first diff-record model. Use JSON Pointer locators for fixture JSON and line locators for generated blocks. Sort records, cap results at 50, report omitted count, and derive any terminal unified diff only from the structured records.
acceptance_criteria:
- Stale diagnostics contain a diff array of records with locator, location kind, change kind, and applicable old or new values.
- Location kinds are JSON Pointer and line; change kinds are added, removed, changed, and type-changed.
- Records sort by locator, cap at 50, and report the omitted count.
- The same structured diff is available in failed gate diagnostic detail; unified text is terminal-only, not machine data.
- Tests cover success, nested objects, arrays, block lines, order, cap, and goldens.

title: Phase 1: validate configuration input
description:
Malformed configuration and Cargo manifest input can currently use defaults or
text scanning that hides invalid state. This can disable gates or apply the
wrong package allowlist. The CLI needs a fail-closed configuration boundary and
a direct command that users can run before preflight.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invalid declared configuration input fails with a Config diagnostic before
  defaults apply.
- `plumb config validate` validates configuration and the Cargo include policy.
- Cargo package include rules come from parsed TOML, not text scanning.
- The capability fixture and contract describe all new codes and the `config`
  verb.

title: Implement strict config and manifest validation
description:
The configuration loader currently accepts invalid shapes as missing values.
The Cargo include allowlist is found by scanning text rather than parsing the
manifest. Both paths can make checks pass when the project input is invalid.
design:
In `src/config.rs`, require the JSON root to be an object and validate every
declared input field when it is present. Keep absent-value defaults, reject
wrong types with `CONFIG_SCHEMA`, treat absent `config_version` as 1, and use
`CONFIG_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` for an integer other than 1. Validate nested
capture, claim, generated-block, tree, environment, and release fields. Claims
must be objects with non-empty `id` and `fixture_path`; their mode is
`value`, `keys`, or `set`, and `keys` or `set` requires an array of strings.
Replace the silent optional string-vector helper with a strict helper.

Add the `config validate` subcommand in `src/main.rs` and the capabilities
model. It loads the strict configuration and parses the manifest policy, then
prints a human-readable success summary. Missing or invalid subcommands return
`USAGE`; failures return the first Config diagnostic and no stdout.

Add the `toml` dependency. In `src/engine.rs`, parse `Cargo.toml` and read
`package.include` as a non-empty array of strings, after removing leading
slashes from globs. Use `CARGO_MANIFEST_INVALID` for unreadable or malformed
TOML, missing or empty include lists, an exclude-only manifest, and non-string
elements. Do not change glob matching or the package-file truth from
`cargo package --list`. Update dependency-count comments in `Cargo.toml` and
`src/config.rs`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Non-object config roots, wrong present field types, malformed claims, and
  invalid nested generated fields return `CONFIG_SCHEMA`.
- `config_version` accepts absent and integer 1, rejects non-integers with
  `CONFIG_SCHEMA`, and rejects other integers with
  `CONFIG_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`.
- Unknown top-level keys remain accepted.
- `plumb config validate` accepts only `validate` as the `config` subcommand
  and shows a success summary only after config and manifest validation pass.
- Cargo include lists are read from TOML and invalid policy states return
  `CARGO_MANIFEST_INVALID`.
- `toml` is the only dependency added by this phase.

title: Add Phase 1 unit tests
description:
Strict input validation needs focused regression tests so later changes cannot
restore silent defaults or text-based manifest parsing.
design:
Add module tests for absent, valid, empty, scalar, array, null, and malformed
forms of optional config blocks. Cover root values, capture fields, version
type-before-value behavior, claims, generated entries, trees, environments,
and release fields. Add manifest fixtures for comments and descriptions that
contain `include`, exclude-only manifests, multiline arrays, malformed TOML,
and true include-list extraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests prove non-object roots cannot disable a gate.
- Tests cover valid and invalid `config_version` values and all claim mode

- Tests prove valid version-one project configuration still loads.
- Tests prove manifest parsing ignores unrelated text containing `include` and

title: Add Phase 1 CLI tests

title: Implement Cargo artifact executable resolution
description:
Path guessing can run the wrong executable or no executable at all. Cargo
already reports the built executable paths, so the tool must retain and use
those records through capture and rendering.
design:
Change `run_build` to return `Executables`: `Cargo` holds a name-to-list map
of artifact paths and `Legacy` marks non-Cargo builds. Treat a build as Cargo
only when `build[0]` is the literal `cargo`. For Cargo builds, add or validate
one JSON `--message-format`, parse stdout line by line, and collect non-null
`compiler-artifact` executable values by target name. Keep stderr inherited.
Return existing `BUILD_FAILED` on non-zero build status.

Add `BIN_NOT_BUILT` and `BIN_AMBIGUOUS`. Cargo lookup with zero paths returns
the first; lookup with more than one path returns the second. Legacy builds use
the existing `target/debug/<name>` fallback. Split command execution into a
resolved-path capture helper. Build once per command path, retain the map for
capture and all generated renders, and resolve each render command by its own
first command token. Change render helpers to accept a resolved path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cargo artifact records, not guessed paths, select capture and render
  executables.
- A Cargo invocation has exactly one valid JSON message-format option; invalid,
  repeated, or valueless forms return `CONFIG_SCHEMA` before Cargo runs.
- Cargo lookup returns `BIN_NOT_BUILT` for zero paths and `BIN_AMBIGUOUS` for
  multiple paths with the same target name.
- Non-Cargo builds preserve the legacy fallback without a panic.
- A command builds once before its capture and render operations.

title: Add Phase 2 unit tests

The Cargo argument rewrite and executable lookup rules have edge cases that

design:
Test message-format rewriting for absent, accepted JSON forms, a non-JSON

and Legacy resolution separately, including zero and multiple artifact paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests prove an absent message format is appended once.
- Tests prove accepted JSON forms are not doubled.
- Tests prove invalid, duplicate, and valueless forms return `CONFIG_SCHEMA`.
- Tests prove empty Cargo artifacts and Legacy builds follow different lookup

- Tests prove duplicate target names return `BIN_AMBIGUOUS`.

title: Add Phase 2 integration tests
description:
Artifact resolution must be proven against real Cargo output, where workspace
and profile paths differ from the legacy debug path.
design:
Create gated integration fixtures that run real locked Cargo builds. Cover a
workspace member, a custom `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, a release-profile build, a
Cargo build with no selected binary, a non-Cargo wrapper build, and two
packages that emit the same binary target name.

- A workspace member binary, a custom target directory binary, and a release

- A Cargo build with no matching binary returns `BIN_NOT_BUILT`.
- A wrapper build uses Legacy behavior without a panic.
- Two built binaries with the same name return `BIN_AMBIGUOUS`.
- The integration tests use the suite's established Cargo-test gating and stay

title: Phase 3: add JSON automation reports
description:
Automation cannot reliably parse the human output from `preflight` and
`release`, including failures that occur before command dispatch. The tool
needs a versioned JSON envelope that reports complete gate, check, and step
state while preserving normal text output by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- `preflight` and `release` support `--format text|json`.
- JSON output is valid on success and every failure path for those commands.
- Preflight records every gate and release records reached checks, preflight,
  and state-changing steps.
- The report contract is described by capabilities and protected by drift
  tests.

Release embeds preflight records and reports reached checks and completed state-changing steps."],"preferences":["Treat report version, field names, ids, status values, code values, and exit values as stable. title: Implement JSON report model and renderers
description:
The current command flow prints evaluation results as it runs. That prevents a
complete machine-readable result and loses JSON formatting on early failures.
Evaluation must produce data before a renderer writes output.
design:
Parse `--format text|json` before config loading, only for `preflight` and
`release`; reject other uses and unknown values with `USAGE`. Extract the
capabilities envelope builder so reports reuse `ok`, tool version, volatile
meta, commands, warnings, errors, and a one-element data array. Define error
records with code, uppercase diagnostic family, exit, and message. JSON failure
before payload creation uses `data: [null]` and one leaf error.

Refactor preflight into evaluation that builds five gate records and rendering
that writes text or JSON. Gate records use stable ids, lowercase status, an
optional leaf code, message, and elapsed time. Always include every gate; use
`skipped` with a reason when a gate does not apply. A failed preflight has an
aggregate `PREFLIGHT_FAILED` envelope error and per-gate leaf codes.

Change release execution to return a populated outcome plus an optional stop
diagnostic. Embed the unrendered preflight report, record only reached checks,
and record only completed state-changing tag and push steps. Populate all
release payload fields on early failure with the specified null or empty value.
Render the outcome once and preserve release ordering and runner boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--format json` produces parseable stdout and routes human diagnostics to
  stderr for every preflight and release failure path, including config-load
  and root-resolution failures.
- Envelope invariants hold: success has status pass, exit 0, and no errors;
  failure has one top-level error, false `ok`, and a matching exit value.
- Preflight JSON contains all five gate ids with `pass`, `fail`, or `skipped`.
- Release JSON contains the required v1 fields, only reached checks and steps,
  and its embedded preflight gates without rendering a second report.
- Text remains the default; skipped gates add readable text output.

title: Add Phase 3 unit tests
description:
The report envelope, status rules, and partial release outcome have strict
machine-facing semantics that need focused tests independent of full CLI runs.
design:
Test envelope error records and invariants, gate-record status serialization,
preflight evaluation and skipped records, and release outcomes that stop before
tagging, after local tagging, or after atomic push. Normalize volatile meta,
crate-root, and elapsed-time values in assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests prove success and failure envelope invariants.
- Tests prove all five gate records are present and skipped gates have reasons.
- Tests prove a failed gate keeps its leaf code while the envelope reports the
  aggregate failure.
- Tests prove release steps describe exactly the completed state changes.

title: Add Phase 3 CLI tests
description:
The JSON promise is an external CLI contract. Binary tests must prove that
stdout remains JSON-only on successful and failing command paths.
design:
Run preflight in text and JSON formats for passing, mixed-failure, and
contract-less configurations. Run release JSON for failures before tagging,
after local tag creation, and after atomic push. Include a valid configuration
with no release block, then assert the early-failure null and empty values.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preflight JSON parses with no progress text on stdout.
- Mixed gate failures retain leaf codes and the top-level aggregate error.
- Text output remains the default and prints leaf codes.
- Release JSON with no release configuration exits 1, reports
  `RELEASE_CONFIG_MISSING`, uses null for unavailable release fields, and uses
  empty checks and steps.
- Release step records reflect failures before tagging, after tagging, and
  after atomic push.

title: Update Phase 3 self-contract
description:
The report schema has stable fields and vocabularies that automation needs to
discover through capabilities and protect through the fixture.
design:
Add `--format` to the preflight and release capability flags and contract table.
Add report version, gate/check/step id vocabularies, and their distinct status
vocabularies to `value_domains`. Regenerate the fixture. Do not add diagnostic
codes in this phase.
acceptance_criteria:
- Capabilities list `--format` only for preflight and release.
- Capabilities value domains include report version, all report ids, and the
  gate/check statuses `pass|fail|skipped` plus step statuses
  `pass|fail|planned`.
- The fixture and `CONTRACT.md` match live capabilities.
- Drift tests detect changes to report contract data.

title: Automate guarded crate releases
description: Rust crate releases need one deliberate local action that verifies the release candidate before it creates a version tag. Publication must remain a visible CI operation after the tag checks pass.
design: Add a `plumb release` command that validates a committed crate release, creates an annotated `v<version>` tag, and pushes the checked branch and tag together. Keep local crate publication outside this command. Add a tag-driven CI workflow that reruns preflight before publication and creates the source release entry only after publication succeeds.
acceptance_criteria:
- `plumb release` verifies the release candidate before it creates a tag.
- The local command does not run non-dry-run `cargo publish`.
- The version tag is annotated and is pushed with a branch consistency check.
- CI reruns preflight before publication and creates the source release entry only after publication succeeds.
notes: CLOSED: The release command, release tests, documentation, self-contract, and tag release workflow are complete. The local command performs only a publish dry run; CI performs publication after tag validation.
close_reason: Release automation complete: configuration and diagnostics bd8172f, guarded command d65802e, tests 89abb71, documentation 5b82a22, self-contract f57ad97, workflow fbd5e7b

title: Add release configuration and diagnostics
description: The release command needs declared branch and remote settings plus stable diagnostics that distinguish configuration, environment, and release-candidate failures.
design: Add an optional `release` object to the project configuration with nonempty `branch` and `remote` strings. An absent object remains valid for existing verbs; `release` rejects it with `RELEASE_CONFIG_MISSING`. A declared non-object or incomplete object is a configuration-schema error. Add the new release diagnostics to the existing families, including separate codes for a Cargo launch failure and a started dry run that fails.
acceptance_criteria:
Existing configurations without a release object load for existing verbs.
The release handler can use RELEASE_CONFIG_MISSING when no release object is declared.
A declared release object requires nonempty string branch and remote fields.
New diagnostics preserve the existing family and exit-code rules.
Configuration tests cover valid, absent, incomplete, mistyped, and empty release settings.
notes: CLOSED: Added optional release configuration, validated declared branch and remote settings, and added the release diagnostic catalog. Configuration tests pass.
close_reason: Added optional release configuration validation and diagnostics — commit bd8172f

comments.author: dave
comments.text: Updated acceptance because command dispatch belongs to the dependent release-command Bead. This Bead now verifies the configuration and diagnostic contract that dispatch uses.

title: Implement release validation
description: A tag is hard to correct after it is pushed. The command needs a deterministic release-validation sequence that leaves the repository unchanged until every check passes.
design: Add a release module and a private command-runner boundary for Git and Cargo. Require a clean worktree, an attached configured branch, and an upstream with zero ahead and behind counts. Read the root package version through `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1`. Require a matching H2 entry in `CHANGELOG.md`; accept exact plain or bracketed version headings with optional summary text. Reject an existing local or remote `v<version>` tag. Reuse the in-process preflight function, then run `cargo publish --dry-run --locked`. After all checks, create `git tag -a v<version> -m v<version>` and use an atomic Git push containing the configured branch ref and tag ref. Report the commit, tag, remote name, and remote URL. Do not use a shell or run a non-dry-run publish command.
acceptance_criteria:
- No tag is created when any check before tag creation fails.
- The command rejects a dirty tree, wrong or detached branch, unsynchronized upstream, missing changelog entry, existing tag, failed preflight, or failed locked dry run.
- A missing changelog maps to `CHANGELOG_VERSION_MISSING`.
- A Cargo launch failure maps to `CARGO_UNAVAILABLE`; a nonzero started dry run maps to `PUBLISH_DRY_RUN_FAILED`.
- Success creates an annotated `v<version>` tag and atomically pushes the configured branch ref and tag ref.
- A failed push leaves the local tag in place and does not delete it.
notes: CLOSED: Added the guarded release sequence. It checks the release candidate before tag creation, uses only dry-run publication, creates an annotated tag, and uses an atomic push. Release behavior tests are tracked separately.
close_reason: Implemented guarded release validation, annotated tagging, and atomic push — commit d65802e

title: Add the release command contract
description: Users and automation need the new release action to appear in the CLI help and machine-readable capability contract.
design: Accept `plumb [--config <path>] release` after configuration loads. Add `release` to the usage text, capability command list, and capability verb map. Mark it as not needing a capture fixture because it needs release configuration instead. Add the release diagnostics to the generated error-code catalog and document the command contract and no-local-publish boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- `plumb release` dispatches through the loaded project configuration.
- Usage output and capabilities list the release verb.
- Capabilities describe `release` without claiming that it needs a capture fixture.
- The capabilities error-code catalog contains every new release diagnostic.
- The command documentation states that local publication is not performed.
notes: CLOSED: Added release to CLI help and machine-readable capabilities. The capability record marks release as independent of a capture fixture and lists its diagnostic codes.
close_reason: Added release CLI and capability contract — commit 6ddf9d2

title: Test guarded release behavior
description: Release checks and the final tag push have failure paths that must remain safe and deterministic without relying on a registry service or a timing race.
design: Test parsers and command order with a fake runner that returns status, stdout, stderr, and launch errors. Cover metadata selection, changelog headings, tag results, branch state, and each release diagnostic. Use temporary Git repositories and a bare local remote for a success test. For push failure, use a mixed runner that delegates real Git operations through local tag creation and then fails only the final atomic push.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests verify the exact `cargo publish --dry-run --locked` and atomic push argument vectors.
- Tests prove the command never invokes a non-dry-run `cargo publish`.
- Tests cover each validation failure and its diagnostic code.
- The success test proves an annotated local tag and matching remote tag.
- The simulated push-failure test proves that the local tag remains and no remote tag is created.
- Tests do not require network access or registry credentials.
notes: CLOSED: Added command-runner tests for validation order, exact publish and push arguments, dry-run-only behavior, and release diagnostic codes. Added temporary local Git repository tests for annotated tag success and failed push behavior without network or registry access.
close_reason: Added guarded release command and local Git repository tests — commit 89abb71

title: Document release operation
description: Release operators need clear instructions about what the new command verifies, what they must prepare first, and which system performs publication.
design: Document the release configuration, validation sequence, annotated-tag action, and no-local-publish boundary in the README and contract reference. State that the operator first commits the version and changelog entry, then runs `plumb release`. Add a root `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the release-command version. Keep that changelog outside the crate package include list because it is release control material, not a shipped crate surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- README documents the release configuration and local command behavior.
- The operator procedure requires a committed version and changelog update before `plumb release`.
- The contract reference lists the new verb and diagnostics.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry for the version that first uses the command.
- The changelog does not enter the crate package file list.
notes: CLOSED: Documented the guarded local release procedure, release settings, and CI publication boundary. Added the 0.0.2 changelog entry and kept the changelog outside the Cargo include list.
close_reason: Documented the guarded release operation and added the 0.0.2 changelog — commit 5b82a22

title: Reconcile plumb self-contract
description: Plumbline checks its own published command surface. A new verb and diagnostic codes must update both the captured capability data and the exact-set claims that guard it.
design: Add `release` to the `verb_set` expected array and every new release diagnostic to the `error_code_set` expected array in `plumbline.json`. These keys are exact sets, so capture alone cannot reconcile them. Update the capabilities fixture and tests after the command output changes. Run capture only when the fixture, claims, contract, and documentation are ready to commit together.
acceptance_criteria:
- `verb_set` contains the complete command-key set, including `release`.
- `error_code_set` contains every emitted diagnostic code, including release codes.
- The capabilities fixture and tests match the updated command surface.
- `plumb check`, `plumb capture --check`, and `plumb preflight` pass on a clean tree.
notes: CLOSED: Updated the exact self-contract command and diagnostic sets, release configuration, and captured capability fixture for version 0.0.2. The self-check and capture check pass; preflight will run after the tracker commit produces a clean tree.
close_reason: Reconciled release capability fixture and exact self-claims — commit f57ad97

title: Add tag release workflow
description: After the verified tag is pushed, CI must repeat release checks before it publishes the crate and creates the source release entry.
design: Add a GitHub Actions workflow for pushed `v*` tags. Check out the tag, install an exact reviewed plumbline version with a locked install, run `plumb preflight`, then run `cargo publish --locked`. Create the GitHub Release only after publication succeeds. Grant only the workflow permissions needed to create that release entry.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pushed `v*` tag starts the release workflow.
- The workflow runs preflight before publication.
- The workflow uses a locked plumbline install and a locked Cargo publish.
- A failed preflight or publish does not create a GitHub Release.
- A successful publish creates the GitHub Release.
notes: CLOSED: Added a v-tag workflow that installs the checked source with a locked install, runs preflight, publishes with a lockfile, and creates the GitHub Release only after publish succeeds.
close_reason: Added tag-driven preflight, publish, and GitHub Release workflow — commit fbd5e7b
